reason: E1 supports that preheating and rare-earth additions like CeO2 refine grains and inhibit cracking, and E2 confirms CeO2 can suppress cracks and refine microstructure, but E3 shows CoCrFeNiMo0.85 deposited by laser on stainless steel was prone to manufacturing cracking, directly contradicting the premise of a crack-free HEA layer. E4 only generally supports laser cladding benefits without addressing the specific HEA or CeO2 combination. Thus, key premises on crack elimination and HEA compatibility are partially contradicted by the cited evidence.
premises: Laser cladding with low heat input limits HAZ and reduces hot cracking
Nano-CeO2 addition refines grain structure and improves coating quality
Substrate preheating and controlled cooling mitigate thermal stress and cracking
CoCrFeNiMo-based HEA can be deposited crack-free on stainless steel by laser methods
The combined process yields superior hardness, wear, and corrosion resistance vs. fusion welds and untreated surfaces
